text: The passage repays attention chiefly by what it withholds. Sarah has no place in Genesis 22, and her death is announced in the verse that follows it; the scene intimates, though it never declares, that the household has not come down from the mountain entire. Abraham returns to the servants, and Isaac is no longer named. Where an inferior narrative would have dwelt upon the return, this narrator withdraws; that silence bears meaning, and leaves Abraham before the servants.
